lines: This is SANT. It turns a few quick, imperfect human demos into a robot that actually works. Let's walk through it, from the moment the site loads.
The story starts with the problem. Robots learn by copying demonstrations, and they need hundreds. Good ones are expensive. Cheap ones, from a mouse or a webcam, are messy.
So we built SANT: Simulate, Augment, Neaten, Train. Every demo is replayed in NVIDIA Isaac Lab, repaired where physics says no, and multiplied into verified copies.
Nemotron, on Nebius Token Factory, proposes. Physics verifies. And the results load as you go: zero out of forty, copied directly. Thirty out of forty, through SANT.
At the end of the descent, the workshop builds itself, piece by piece. This is where all the work happens.
The shelf holds every job as a cartridge: record, perfect, multiply, train.
Plug one into the machine, and it projects the robot, replaying a real, physics-checked demo.
At the bench, you make your own cartridge: pick a shell, a colour, the robot it runs on, and give it a name.
The wall shows the arms SANT has run in Isaac, and the ones planned next.
And the proof screen steps through how we know it works, with every number sourced.
Now, live. Record connects to a Franka arm running in NVIDIA Isaac Lab, and I drive it with the keyboard.
This is Isaac Lab itself. Down to the cube, grab it, carry it to the bin, and let go.
SANT reviews the take on the spot: the cube is in the bin, no pushing, one millimetre off centre. Pass.
Scenes can come from a sentence. Nemotron writes the plan, and code checks it before it ever reaches the robot.
Then, Run SANT. Today, I'll stop at the data.
Isaac replays the demo with real contact forces. Verified.
Then it multiplies it. The cube and the bin move, every copy is replayed, and only the ones that pass are kept. Ten out of ten, from one demo.
The test track replays all forty final runs, straight from Isaac. Thirty succeed. Every failure dropped the cube, and that's what we fix next.
Next, we want SANT to take any robot file. Bring your own robot's model and train it in SANT, so anyone passionate about robotics can teach their robot, without the cost of a lab.
A few human demos in. A robot that works out. This is SANT.
